newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian 10-yr bond looking for break.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian 10-yr bond looking for break.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond contract ended SYCOM trading at 92.345, matching last Friday's 10-week peak, and gearing the market up for a further advance going into the Federal budget.
*SFE open for budget session 7.00-8.15 p.m. (0900-1015 GMT).
The expectation that the Australian bond market will rally into what is likely to to be a favourable Federal budget appears to be going to plan.

The June 10-year bond futures contract ended after hours trading testing 92.345, a 10-week high seen briefly on Friday, gearing the market for a further advance with initial resistance seen at 92.410 and then 92.480, analysts said.

The market had failed to breach 92.340 in Friday's SYCOM session and Monday's dayside trade, but the firm after hours close now sets up the contract for a test of 92.410 and a break out of the rising mini-channel that started in late April.
The 10-year contract ended Monday's pit session at 92.320.
A firm bias in U.S. Treasuries helped to underpin the local market, overcoming concerns over the recent weakness of the U.S. dollar against the yen.
The U.S. market ran into profit-taking going into the close, but expectations of weak economic data this week for retail sales and inflation limited the retracement.

Meanwhile, Treasurer Peter Costello will hand down the 1997/98 budget at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT), which is expected to include a substantial headline budget surplus, lessening the need for bond issuance in the forthcoming fiscal year.
